summary: Algae example differs from the cited verb and may belong to qyš

summary: New idiom: qayṣat qarʕi 'du magst mir den Kopf scheren' (Anredeformel)

data.headword: qayṣat qarʕi 'du magst mir den Kopf scheren' (Anredeformel)
data.turoyo: Məlla: “Qayṣat qarʕi! Həngi d mərralli w ʕabiro i zuḥṯo b lebi, məlli šrolo yo, marfelilux. Annaqqa lə gmarfallux.”
data.translation: Sie sprach: "Du magst mir den Kopfscheren entschuldige mich. Weil sie so viel auf mich einredeten, und ich Angst kriegte, dachte ich, es sei wahr, und habe dich losgelassen. Diesmal werde ich dich nichtloslassen."

rationale: Repeated at 61/294 and 61/331; targeted glossary search returned no idiom. Preserve the literal edition rendering and ask about pragmatic force.

summary: The entry uses one shared sense list: active 1 cutting and 2 shearing can also be Detransitive, while 3 pathological condition and 4 heart-based suspicion are marked (Detrans.) within that list. Do not introduce an independent D-numbering system.

Cutting sheet metal, iron, edible sheets, grape bunches and an arm changes the patient, not the lexical meaning. Haircut threats and ordinary shearing remain I.2; no separate beheading sense is inferred from a German haircut threat.

JTM 1.1/90 provides an agentless Detransitive shearing Infectum with wool as subject. Compare lexical Detransitive heart-suspicion and pathological foot states; inherited 52/76 and 96/21 are not added again.

qyoṣo at 45/13 is an unambiguous action nominal with d-patient and populates Nomen Actionis. qyoṣo du+sawko in occupation discourse may name the activity or the worker; keep the qayoṣo alternation for review rather than using it to reconstruct a paradigm.
PrS 26/12 repeats the inherited ulcer quotation (prs63/12), but the supplied German says broken. Preserve the edition and ask; no silent replacement by the glossary translation.
